conversation.content: I'm 78 and I have many problems. My heart, my arthritis, my eyes.

Thank you so much for coming in today — it sounds like you're managing quite a lot, and I want to make sure we cover everything properly for you.

To start us off, which of those problems is bothering you the most right now, or is there something new that brought you in today?
My shortness of breath has been worse this week.

I'm sorry to hear that — it must be quite uncomfortable and worrying for you.

Can you tell me, did the breathlessness come on suddenly, or has it been getting worse gradually over this week?
It's worst when I walk to the kitchen. I have to stop and rest.

That sounds really exhausting — having to stop just to walk to the kitchen must make things very difficult at home.

Has this breathlessness been there for a while and just got worse this week, or is it completely new?
I've had swollen ankles for about 2 months. My socks leave marks.

Thank you for telling me that — that's really helpful to know.

I'll make sure we come back to the breathlessness in more detail, but since you've mentioned the swollen ankles — has the swelling been in both ankles, or just one side?
I sleep with 3 pillows otherwise I can't breathe.

Thank you for telling me that — that's very important information for the doctor.

Do you ever wake up at night suddenly feeling short of breath, or feeling like you need to sit up or get some air?
I take furosemide 40mg, enalapril 10mg, digoxin 0.125mg, and warfarin 5mg.

Thank you so much for knowing all of your medicines — that's really helpful.

I do want to come back to ask about each of those medicines in a bit more detail, but first — do you ever get any chest pain or tightness along with the breathlessness?
I also take amlodipine 5mg and aspirin 75mg.

Thank you, that's very useful — I've noted all of those medicines and I'll come back to ask about each one shortly.

Do you ever get any chest pain or tightness along with the breathlessness?
I live with my daughter.

That's lovely to hear — it's good to know you have family support at home.

Do you ever get any chest pain or tightness along with the breathlessness?
I've fallen twice in the past 6 months. Both times I was dizzy first.

Oh, I'm sorry to hear that — two falls is really concerning, and the dizziness beforehand is very important for the doctor to know about.

When you felt dizzy before the falls, did you actually black out or lose consciousness at all, or did you stay awake throughout?
My memory — my daughter says I repeat things. I don't always remember what I ate yesterday.

Thank you for sharing that — it takes courage to talk about that, and it's really important for the doctor to know.

I want to make sure we come back to both the falls and the memory changes in more detail. But first, let me return to something I asked earlier — do you ever get any chest pain or tightness along with the breathlessness?
I'm not too sad. I miss my independence though.

I completely understand — losing some of your independence can be really hard, and it makes a lot of sense that you'd miss it.

I hear you, and I'll make sure the doctor knows how you're feeling about that. Now, coming back to what I asked — do you ever get any chest pain or tightness when you feel breathless?
